title: Starlane transition digest - night->morning handoff (2028-06-14)
content:
SUMMARY:
Night shift (2200-0600 UTC) observed two related issues between 01:12 and 02:04 UTC that impacted 95th percentile tail latency for text-generation routes and caused elevated 5xx rates for a 18-minute window. Nothing customer-visible beyond increased latencies and a handful of retries from internal canaries. No P0 raised, but we opened SRE-8421 to track root cause and follow-ups.

TIMELINE (UTC):
- 01:12 - Prometheus alert: serving_runtime_high_tail_latency (p95 > 450ms for 3 min). Alert routed to #sre-night.
- 01:14 - On-call (Maya) acknowledged, started triage. Initial check: autoscaler activity, GPU pool health, and gateway error rates.
- 01:17 - Brief spike in backend 502/503 from model-proxy observed; correlated with a burst of cache invalidation jobs kicked by a deployment job.
- 01:20 - Rolled back last config change to routing weights (Canary 3 -> stable) as quick mitigation; latency improved but 5xx persisted.
- 01:26 - Identified runaway cache invalidation task in jobs-service (job id job-ff7a). Killed job and paused scheduled invalidations.
- 01:30 - 5xx rates falling, p95 returning to baseline.
- 01:40 - Verified that KV cache hit-rate recovered after disabled invalidation; no further 5xx.
- 02:04 - Closed active triage; left SRE-8421 with initial notes and list of follow-ups. Handoff to morning team at 06:15.

INCIDENT NOTES / OBSERVATIONS:
- Root-cause hypothesis: cache invalidation job executed at scale causing thundering key eviction and DB/KV throttling, which increased model-proxy latencies and produced 502/503.
- Contributing factor: invalidation job runs were not throttled by deployment/maintenance window and coincided with model-serving autoscaler rebalancing. Race condition between invalidation flood and autoscaler cold-starts.
- Runbook gap: current runbook for cache-invalidation (confluence:redwood/sre/runbooks/cache-invalidation) assumes small batches; no guidance for full-data invalidation at peak times. Need a throttled-window procedure.
- Observed behavior in metrics: prefix cache hit-rate dropped from 98% -> 52%; model-proxy concurrent connections spiked x3; DB write latency rose 4x.

TEMP MITIGATIONS APPLIED:
- Killed job-ff7a and paused all scheduled full invalidations (command: jobsctl pause --tag full-invalidate).
- Rolled routing weight change back to previous canary to reduce cross-traffic while caches warm.
- Temporarily increased model-proxy connection pool limit to reduce 502 under load (reverted after stability).

FOLLOW-UPS (owners, due dates):
- SRE-8421: Full RCA and timeline (owner: Ethan Cole, due: 2028-06-18).
- Add throttling and staggered schedule to cache-invalidation runbook (owner: Priya Nair, due: 2028-06-20).
- Create automated pre-check that rejects full invalidation outside maintenance window (owner: Luis Martinez, due: 2028-06-25). Ticket: SRE-8439.
- Add dashboard panel for cache-invalidation job rate and job-run overlaps with autoscaler events (owner: Maya Rios, due: 2028-06-21). Grafana panel id: serving-runtime.jobs.cache_invalidate.
- Run a chaos test to validate autoscaler + cache warmup behavior at scale (owner: Eng Reliability, due: 2028-07-05).

RUNBOOK DRAFT NOTES (quick edits to push):
- Immediate additions requested:
  - section: preflight checks before running full invalidation (check p95, autoscaler activity, scheduled deploys).
  - procedure: stagger batches with backoff and a hard rate cap (example CLI: invalidate --batch-size 2k --backoff 30s).
  - emergency rollback: steps to pause invalidation and restore last known-good routing weight.
- Mark step that killing invalidation job requires jobsctl with the --force flag and update RBAC for SRE squad.

COMMUNICATIONS / CUSTOMER NOTES:
- No customer-facing incident was required. Product analytics showed transient increase in retry counts for internal sampling only.
- Notified customer-success and sent summary to internal #infra-status for transparency.

OPEN QUESTIONS / TO FOLLOW UP:
- Is the job scheduler misconfigured to allow overlapping full invalidations? (Priya to audit).
- Do we need a runtime circuit-breaker at model-proxy that can detect downstream KV DB throttling and shed load gracefully?
- Should full invalidation be an operation that requires two-person approval above X key count?

HANDOFF NOTES FOR MORNING TEAM (what I would want to know):
- Watch cache hit-rate panels (serving-runtime.cache.prefix_hit_rate) for any dip below 85%; investigate jobs queue if it dips.
- If 502/503 reappears: check jobs-service for recent runs, kill any full invalidation jobs, then check model-proxy pool usage.
- Check SRE-8421 for latest notes/attachments (I added logs and job timeline).

QUICK TODOS FOR TODAY'S WINDOW (morning):
- Priya: push runbook edits to Confluence and add the preflight checklist.
- Ethan: start RCA doc with annotated graphs (attach to SRE-8421).
- Luis: implement a pre-check gate in jobs-service to prevent full invalidations during high-tail-latency windows.

NOTES TO SELF (Maya):
- Remember to add a short snippet to the runbook about how to interpret model-proxy 502 vs 504 in this context.
- Capture the exact command sequence used to pause invalidations and paste into runbook for reproducibility.

ATTACHMENTS / LINKS (added to ticket):
- raw logs: s3://redwood-logs/sre/2028-06-14/night-ff7a-invalidations.log
- grafana snapshots: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/serving-runtime/snapshot/xyz123
- job trace: jobs-service/trace/job-ff7a

SIGNOFF:
- Night on-call: Maya Rios (m.rios@redwood.com).
- Bridge summary posted to #sre-night at 02:18 UTC.
- Handover to morning on-call scheduled at 06:15 UTC.

END OF DIGEST
